subject.title: No owner role on an org I created

question: After verifying the `xerg` membership and audit history, should maintainers perform a one-off audited ownership repair or ship a reusable guarded repair path for similarly inconsistent organizations?
rationale: Changing organization ownership is security-sensitive, and source inspection alone cannot establish whether this is an isolated production-data inconsistency or a recurring creation-path defect.

options.title: Verify and repair safely
options.body: Inspect the organization, membership, creator identity, and audit records, restore ownership only when provenance is conclusive, and add a reusable repair only if equivalent inconsistent records exist.

options.title: One-off operator repair
options.body: Restore this organization through an audited administrative action and retain the issue until current creation behavior is independently verified.

recommendation.title: Verify and repair safely
recommendation.body: Inspect the organization, membership, creator identity, and audit records, restore ownership only when provenance is conclusive, and add a reusable repair only if equivalent inconsistent records exist.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available project-level routing candidate for a security-sensitive ClawHub ownership decision, though file-level ownership evidence is limited.
